rules: Standalone signals: no case, entity or map-line links. Incident date kept apart from report date; where the source does not say when the failure began, the pin date is the report or notice date and incident_event is 'found'. Pin = the place the source gives; 'approx.' in the title when only a street, area or town is known. An outage pin stands for the affected area when the failure point cannot be mapped, and the location note says so. Sources that reuse one notice or one police statement are not independent corroboration. Being near another pin is not a link. No one is named as a suspect. Planned outages are not pins (owner decision of 23 Oct 2026). Every fact-base quote matched word for word against the saved source text.

signals.title: Seshego Hospital substation, Seshego (approx.): switch stripped, cables damaged, about R500,000; police seek suspects, 11 Oct
signals.content: Police say essential electrical infrastructure at the Seshego Hospital substation on Bookelo Street, Seshego (Capricorn District), was tampered with. The damage was found on Sunday 11 October when a municipal electrician responded at about 17:00 to a complaint about a power supply problem at the hospital. He found the substation doors open and a school bag with a side cutter, a knife and electrical wire inside. A switch had been stripped and damaged, and high-voltage cables and the distribution board were also damaged; the damage is estimated at R500,000. No arrests have been made; police have launched a manhunt for unknown suspects (police statement, published by Review Online on 14 October, with Limpopo Provincial Commissioner Lt-Gen Jan Scheepers quoted). When the tampering happened is not stated; the date is the day it was found. One report, resting on police. The pin is approximate: the hospital point, not the substation itself.

signals.title: Adshade Street bridge over the R71, Tzaneen (approx.): burst asbestos water main, repair waiting on a pipe from Cape Town, reported 19 Oct
signals.content: A water pipe burst along the original pipeline near the Adshade Street bridge over the R71 in Tzaneen, leaving residents with water supply problems (Letaba Herald, 19 October). Greater Tzaneen Municipality DA councillor Chrisma Bredenkamp said the damaged asbestos pipe is being replaced with steel; the replacement pipe has to come from Cape Town. Workers could not reach the section through the tunnel under the bridge and had to open the area above the pipeline. When the pipe burst is not stated, so the date is the report date. The arrival date of the pipe and the completion date were not confirmed; the municipality's spokesperson had not replied by publication. One report. The pin is approximate (street level).

Approximate, street level (about 800 m).

signals.title: Polokwane (approx.): water outage while Pump Station 3 is stopped to repair two pipeline leaks, outside PS2 and at Ga-Maja, about 8 Oct
signals.content: Polokwane Municipality told residents of a water outage after Lepelle Northern Water stopped Pump Station 3 for urgent repairs to two pipeline leaks, one just outside Pump Station 2 and one at Ga-Maja (municipal notice, published by Review Online on 8 October). The repairs were estimated at about eight hours. Affected areas listed include Ga-Chuene, Thokgweng, Polokwane City, Seshego, Nirvana, Bendor, Penina Park and Westenburg, several extensions, Peter Mokaba Stadium and the line to Krugersburg. The date the pump station was stopped is not stated, so the date is the report date. One report, resting on the municipality. The pin is approximate: the Polokwane town point stands for the affected area, not for either leak; Ga-Maja lies about 28 km south of the pin.

checked.incident: About Thu 8 Oct 2026: the notice was published that morning; the day the pump station was stopped is not stated (Polokwane Municipality, via Review Online). Repairs estimated at about eight hours.
checked.reported: 8 Oct 2026 (Review Online, municipal notice); earliest report found
checked.location: Two leaks on the bulk line, one just outside Pump Station 2 and one at Ga-Maja; the outage covered parts of Polokwane (Polokwane Municipality, via Review Online). The pin is the Polokwane town point from the place-name list and stands for the affected area. Neither leak is pinned: Pump Station 2 could not be placed, and Ga-Maja is about 28 km south. Approximate, town level (about 15 km).

signals.title: Musina township (approx.): low water supply after an electrical breakdown leaves several Limpopo River boreholes down, 10 Oct
signals.content: Vhembe District Municipality said on 10 October that several boreholes along the Limpopo River were not working because of an electrical breakdown, cutting water production and leaving Musina Township and surrounding areas with low water supply; repairs had been requested. GroundUp visited Campbell township in Musina on 15 October and found residents queuing with empty containers for municipal water tankers; one resident said her tap had been dry for three months, and residents said supply had been unreliable for years. When the breakdown started is not stated, so the date is the notice date. Two sources: the municipal notice and GroundUp's own reporting, which cites the notice for the cause. The pin is approximate (town level).
